newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR CHELSEA V WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR CHELSEA V WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Facts and figures on Chelsea and Wimbledon, who meet in an F.A. Cup semifinal at Highbury on Sunday:
Chelsea:
Formed 1905.
Major honours: European Cup Winners Cup 1971, English league champions 1955, English F.A. Cup 1970, English League Cup 1965.
Ground: Stamford Bridge, capacity 32,000 during ground development (41,000 after completion).
Player/manager: Ruud Gullit
Record league appearances: Ron Harris 655 (1962-80)
Record league goalscorer: Bobby Tambling 164 (1958-70)
Highest league scorer in one season: Jimmy Greaves 41 (1960-61)
Most capped player: Ray Wilkins 24 (of 84 caps), England
Wimbledon:
Formed 1889 as Wimbledon Old Centrals. Changed name to Wimbledon 1905.
Major honours: English F.A. Cup 1988, English F.A. Amateur Cup 1963.
Ground: Selhurst Park (shared with Crystal Palace), capacity 26,309.
Manager: Joe Kinnear
Record league appearances: Alan Cork 430 (1977-92)
Record league goalscorer: Alan Cork 145 (1977-92)
Highest league scorer in one season: Alan Cork 29 (1983-84)
Most capped player: Vinnie Jones 9, Wales
Previous F.A. Cup meetings:
1995-96 Sixth round (March 9 1996)
Chelsea 2 (Mark Hughes, Ruud Gullit
Wimbledon 2 (Robbie Earle, Dean Holdsworth)
1995-96 Sixth round replay (March 20 1996)
Wimbledon 1 (Jon Goodman)
Chelsea 3 (Dan Petrescu, Mike Duberry, Mark Hughes)
Other facts:

- Wimbledon are the only club to win both the now-defunct F.A. Amateur Cup (1963) and the F.A. Cup (1988). Ironically, Middlesbrough who won the Amateur Cup in 1895 and 1898 could match that achievement this year, possibly by beating Wimbledon in the Cup Final.

- When Wimbledon beat Burnley in an F.A. Cup third round match at Turf Moor on January 4 1975, they became the first non-League team to win away from home in the cup against a team from the top division for 55 years. Wimbledon became a League team two years later.

- Dave Beasant made history twice in one day when Wimbledon won the F.A. Cup in 1988. He was the first goalkeeper ever to captain a winning side and the first man to save a penalty in a Wembley F.A. Cup final.

- Chelsea came close to becoming the only side to play at home in an F.A. Cup Final in 1920 when Stamford Bridge was the venue. Chelsea reached the semifinal but lost 3-1 to Aston Villa who went on to beat Huddersfield 1-0 in the final at the Bridge.
- Peter Osgood was the last player to score a goal in every round of the F.A. Cup when Chelsea won it in 1970. Wimbledon's Robbie Earle can still match that achievement this season.

- When Chelsea beat Leeds United to win the F.A. Cup in 1970 after extra-time in a replay at Old Trafford, they only led for 16 of the 240 minutes of playing time. Leeds led twice in the first match at Wembley which ended in a 2-2 draw and then took the lead for the third time in the tie in the first half of the replay. Chelsea took the lead for the only time when David Webb scored with a header 16 minutes from the end of extra-time and Chelsea hung on to win 2-1.
